primary_devkit_candidate: Raspberry Pi Zero / Pi Zero 2 W SeedSigner-style kit
variant_candidates: Raspberry Pi 3/4/5 for development and accessibility variants

supported_board_targets: Raspberry Pi Zero 1.3 preferred because wireless hardware is absent
Raspberry Pi Zero W only with wireless disabled or physically mitigated
Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W only with wireless disabled or physically mitigated
Raspberry Pi 3/4/5 development variants only if they preserve the same offline QR, display, GPIO button, and RAM-only custody boundary
display_targets: Waveshare 1.3 inch LCD HAT, ST7789, 240x240, SPI
SeedSigner-compatible 240x240 ST7789 display and controls with the same review readability target
camera_targets: Pi Zero-compatible OV5647 camera or ZeroCam-style CSI camera for request QR scanning
control_targets: Waveshare HAT joystick and KEY1/KEY2/KEY3 GPIO button layout
SeedSigner legacy 26-pin GPIO remap only when documented and tested

safety: Reject must take precedence over approve when multiple buttons are pressed.
Touch must not be accepted as approve/reject consent.

os_targets: SeedSigner OS pi0/pi02w Buildroot profile reference
nSealr stateless QR vault OS profile with removable microSD boot media, no swap, no remote access, and wireless disabled or absent
acceptance_targets: Boot and run the nSealr Raspberry QR vault on the user-provided Pi Zero hardware
Scan shared nsealr1 static and animated QR requests through the Pi camera path
Render complete Nostr event review detail pages on the SeedSigner-compatible display before physical approval
Navigate Event, Content, Tags, and Decision pages with SeedSigner-compatible GPIO controls
Display signed-event QR output without using USB data transport for the stateless vault flow

security_requirements: Wireless must be disabled or physically absent in high-assurance Raspberry QR vault builds.
Keep the Raspberry QR vault stateless: seed or key material exists only in RAM during the signing session.
Do not store persistent signing secrets on removable boot media or attached storage.
Keep camera input, display output, local approval, and response QR rendering inside the offline device boundary.
Do not add secure-element, TROPIC01, USB remote-signer, or persistent-secret requirements to the stateless Raspberry QR vault.
review_requirements: Provide a local display large enough to show raw event kind, signer author, complete content, complete tags, request id, and approval_digest.
Provide physical approve and reject controls with distinct tactile actions.
Touch must not be accepted as approve/reject consent.
Require explicit physical approval for each sign_event request.
Reject signing when the displayed request id does not match the pending request.
Reject signing when the displayed approval_digest does not match the pending request review.
Require camera/display/GPIO acceptance tests before a Raspberry hardware build is treated as more than a desktop harness.
qr_requirements: Decode the shared nsealr1 QR envelope from nSealr/specs.
Reject malformed static and animated QR input before trusted review.
Render signed-event QR output only after trusted review and physical approval.
Test scanning at multiple brightness, angle, distance, and display-size conditions.
identity_policy_requirements: Reference the shared nsealr-account-descriptor-v0 route raspberry_qr_vault.
Use policy-manual-only-qr-vault for every stateless QR signing session.
Require persistent_grants: false; no grant store or policy automation belongs to the stateless Raspberry QR vault.
notes: This is a requirements scaffold for Raspberry/Pi kit validation, not a routed PCB or purchase order.
The current implementation has a hardware-neutral adapter boundary; real camera, display, GPIO, OS image, and enclosure validation remain pending.
TROPIC01 belongs to the TROPIC01 universal secure device line, not the stateless Raspberry QR vault.
